decision.observation: Wide view: the gate's left post has two metal plates with horizontal pins protruding: one near the top rail (~0.29, 0.455) and one lower (~0.275, 0.665), the lower one looking like a sliding bolt pin. The right post similarly has plates with a lever (~0.70, 0.44) and a hanging crank (~0.71, 0.63). The white bowl sits behind the bottom rails at ~(0.38, 0.60). The goose stands center-left at ~(0.48, 0.49), beak toward the gate.
decision.hypothesis: The left post's lower horizontal pin may be the sliding bolt that holds the gate; a grab-and-pull on it could unlatch the gate. The goose may be able to path along the near side to the left post.
decision.memory: Have mostly tested right-post hardware; left-post lower bolt pin untested.
